title: Filtering All the Way
endLine: Protein can slow filtration, but cannot reverse it for long.

scenes.tts: Day and night, fluid seeps from your smallest blood vessels into nearby tissue. The textbook says most of it slips back in at the far end. Does it?
scenes.narration: Day and night, fluid seeps from your smallest blood vessels into nearby tissue. The textbook says most of it slips back in at the far end. Does it?
scenes.visual: THE WORLD, built here and kept for the whole film (16:9). COLOUR BY CONCEPT, same in every scene: blood a pale RED fluid with drifting dots flowing left to right; plasma protein (albumin) GOLD dots; the push (pressure driving water out) WHITE arrows and a WHITE bar; the hold-back (protein pulling water in) GOLD arrows and a GOLD bar; water and filtrate pale BLUE drops; the glycocalyx a GREEN fuzzy fibre mat; the textbook line ORANGE dashed; the steady-state curve BLUE solid. LAYOUT: TOP 40% of the frame: one capillary drawn as a long horizontal tube across about 85% of the frame width, its lower wall a row of flat lining cells with narrow gaps between them, a thin GREEN mat lining the inside, label 'arterial end' at the left end and 'venous end' at the right end. Just below the tube a dark band labelled 'tissue'. A WHITE ring, the probe, sits on the tube and marks the point being measured. RIGHT EDGE beside the tube: two vertical bars on one shared hidden scale of 0 to 35 mmHg, labelled 'push' (WHITE) and 'hold-back' (GOLD), each with its number above it (both empty during the hook). BOTTOM 40%: a plot whose x axis 'capillary pressure (mmHg)' runs from 32 at the LEFT to 12 at the RIGHT, linear, placed directly under the tube so each pressure sits under the matching stretch of tube; y axis 'net (mmHg)', -6 to +16, a bold zero line with 'out' written above it and 'in' below it. The plot starts empty. Hook motion: pale BLUE drops seep out of the lower wall along the WHOLE length of the tube and drift down into the tissue band. On 'the textbook', a dashed ORANGE ghost overlays the tube: arrows pointing out at the arterial end, arrows pointing back in at the venous end, labelled 'textbook'. On the question, white text across the top: 'Does it come back?'

Title 'Filtering All the Way' fades in across the top for 2 s while the question text fades out. The ORANGE ghost arrows fade out. Blood keeps flowing left to right; BLUE drops keep seeping slowly into the tissue.

scenes.tts: Start with the push: pressure inside minus pressure outside. In resting muscle, take eighteen millimeters of mercury inside and about minus one outside. The push is nineteen.
scenes.narration: Start with the push: pressure inside minus pressure outside. In resting muscle, take 18 mmHg inside and about -1 outside. The push is 19.
scenes.caption: Start with the push: pressure inside minus pressure outside. In resting muscle, take 18 mmHg inside and about -1 outside. The push is 19.
scenes.visual: The WHITE probe ring slides to the 18 mmHg point of the tube (under it, the x axis tick 18), labelled 'resting muscle'. Tag 'teaching numbers' appears at bottom right and stays all film. On 'eighteen', a label 'inside 18' appears on the tube at the probe; on 'minus one', a label 'tissue -1' appears in the tissue band below it. A WHITE arrow grows downward out of the wall at the probe, and on 'nineteen' the WHITE 'push' bar fills to 19 with '19' above it. BLUE drops at the probe are nudged outward along the arrow.

scenes.tts: Now the hold-back. Plasma proteins, mostly albumin, pull water toward the blood with about twenty-six. Protein just past the wall's sugary lining, the glycocalyx, pulls back with six.
scenes.narration: Now the hold-back. Plasma proteins, mostly albumin, pull water toward the blood with about 26. Protein just past the wall's sugary lining, the glycocalyx, pulls back with 6.
scenes.caption: Now the hold-back. Plasma proteins, mostly albumin, pull water toward the blood with about 26. Protein just past the wall's sugary lining, the glycocalyx, pulls back with 6.
scenes.visual: On 'plasma proteins', the GOLD dots inside the tube brighten and small GOLD arrows point from the tissue up into the tube at the probe; label 'plasma 26'. On 'sugary lining', the GREEN mat along the inside of the wall glows along its whole length, label 'glycocalyx'. On 'pulls back with six', a few GOLD dots appear just on the tissue side of the wall at the probe, label 'outside 6', with one small GOLD arrow pointing back down. Beside the bars, the GOLD 'hold-back' bar shows an OUTLINE at height 20 (26 minus 6), labelled '26 - 6 = 20', not yet filled. The WHITE push bar stays at 19.

scenes.tts: The wall lets a little albumin through, so that difference counts at about nine tenths: eighteen. Push nineteen, hold-back eighteen. The net is one, outward.
scenes.narration: The wall lets a little albumin through, so that difference counts at about nine tenths: eighteen. Push nineteen, hold-back eighteen. The net is one, outward.
scenes.visual: On 'lets a little albumin through', two GOLD dots slip slowly through a gap in the wall into the tissue. On 'nine tenths', the GOLD bar fills to 18 inside its outline of 20 (the top tenth stays empty), label '0.9 x 20 = 18'. On 'push nineteen, hold-back eighteen', the two bars stand side by side, 19 and 18, and the 1-unit difference at the top of the WHITE bar glows. On 'one, outward', a single BLUE drop leaves the wall at the probe, and a BLUE dot is placed on the plot at x = 18, y = +1, labelled 'rest: +1'. (Check: 18 - (-1) - 0.9 x (26 - 6) = +1.)

scenes.tts: Pressure falls along the capillary, from about thirty-two to twelve. Keep the hold-back at eighteen. The arterial end nets fifteen outward, the venous end five inward. That's the textbook picture.
scenes.narration: Pressure falls along the capillary, from about 32 to 12. Keep the hold-back at 18. The arterial end nets 15 outward, the venous end 5 inward. That's the textbook picture.
scenes.caption: Pressure falls along the capillary, from about 32 to 12. Keep the hold-back at 18. The arterial end nets 15 outward, the venous end 5 inward. That's the textbook picture.
scenes.visual: On 'falls along the capillary', a WHITE pressure ribbon runs along the tube, bright at the left and dimmer to the right, labels '32' at the arterial end and '12' at the venous end. On 'keep the hold-back at eighteen', the GOLD bar locks at 18 with a small padlock tag 'fixed'. The probe slides to the arterial end: the WHITE bar grows to 33, net '+15', an ORANGE point plotted at (32, +15), BLUE drops pour out strongly there. The probe slides to the venous end: the WHITE bar shrinks to 13, net '-5', an ORANGE point at (12, -5), and BLUE drops flow back IN from the tissue there. On 'textbook picture', a dashed ORANGE straight line draws through (32, +15), (24, +7), (20, +3), (16, -1), (12, -5), crossing zero at 17, labelled 'textbook'.

scenes.tts: But that sum held the outside protein fixed. Zoom in on one gap between lining cells. The glycocalyx covers its mouth like a sieve, over a thin film of fluid.
scenes.narration: But that sum held the outside protein fixed. Zoom in on one gap between lining cells. The glycocalyx covers its mouth like a sieve, over a thin film of fluid.
scenes.visual: On 'held the outside protein fixed', the padlock on the GOLD bar flashes. On 'zoom in', the camera dives into one gap in the lower wall near the middle of the tube: two lining cells now fill about 65% of the frame height, blood above them, tissue below, the narrow gap running down between them. The plot shrinks to a small inset at top right, still showing the ORANGE line and the BLUE rest point; the two bars stay, smaller, at the right edge. On 'like a sieve', the GREEN fibre mat lies across the mouth of the gap on the blood side, label 'glycocalyx'. On 'thin film', a thin pocket of fluid just beneath the mat, inside the gap, is outlined and labelled 'thin film', holding about 6 GOLD dots.

scenes.tts: When the vessel filters, nearly protein-free fluid streams out through the gap. It rinses the film, so protein there stays low, and the hold-back stays strong.
scenes.narration: When the vessel filters, nearly protein-free fluid streams out through the gap. It rinses the film, so protein there stays low, and the hold-back stays strong.
scenes.visual: A stream of pale BLUE drops passes down through the GREEN mat, through the thin film and out of the gap into the tissue. GOLD dots in the plasma bump against the mat and stay above it. On 'rinses the film', the few GOLD dots in the film are carried downstream out of the gap, leaving 3 or 4 behind; label 'rinsed'. As the stream starts, the WHITE push bar at the right rises to just above the GOLD bar (no new number shown), because outward flow needs push above hold-back. On 'hold-back stays strong', the GOLD bar at the right glows, steady at 18.

scenes.tts: Now reverse the stream. When a vessel absorbs, water leaves the film for the blood, but the protein stays behind. It piles up, and the hold-back weakens.
scenes.narration: Now reverse the stream. When a vessel absorbs, water leaves the film for the blood, but the protein stays behind. It piles up, and the hold-back weakens.
scenes.visual: On 'reverse the stream', the WHITE push bar drops below the GOLD bar (no new number shown), and the BLUE drops turn and move UP the gap, through the mat, into the blood. GOLD dots arriving from the tissue are stopped under the mat and collect in the thin film; on 'piles up', the film fills with GOLD dots (from 4 to about 14), label 'left behind'. On 'hold-back weakens', the GOLD bar at the right shrinks until it is level with the WHITE push bar, and the upward BLUE stream slows to a stop.

scenes.tts: Here is the one idea. The hold-back is set by the flow itself. Filtering keeps it strong. Absorbing weakens it until absorption stops.
scenes.narration: Here is the one idea. The hold-back is set by the flow itself. Filtering keeps it strong. Absorbing weakens it until absorption stops.
scenes.visual: Split the cleft view into two side-by-side copies of the same gap. LEFT copy: BLUE stream down and out, film nearly empty of GOLD, GOLD bar tall, label 'filtering: strong'. RIGHT copy: BLUE stream up, then stopped, film crowded with GOLD, GOLD bar short, label 'absorbing: weakens'. On 'set by the flow itself', a white label spans both: 'hold-back set by flow'. On 'absorption stops', the RIGHT copy's stream freezes and a small 'stop' tag appears.

scenes.tts: Now the venous end, where the push is only thirteen. In the steady state, does it absorb, filter, or sit at exactly zero?
scenes.narration: Now the venous end, where the push is only 13. In the steady state, does it absorb, filter, or sit at exactly zero?
scenes.caption: Now the venous end, where the push is only 13. In the steady state, does it absorb, filter, or sit at exactly zero?
scenes.visual: Pull back out of the cleft to the full tube; the plot grows back to full size at the bottom. The WHITE probe slides to the venous end; the WHITE bar reads 13. A tag 'steady state' appears top left and stays to the end of the film. On the question, three white choices appear across the top: 'absorb?  filter?  zero?'
Predict pause. The question card stays. Blood keeps flowing; the probe sits at the venous end; the WHITE bar holds at 13 and the GOLD bar flickers between 12 and 14 without settling. No other change.

scenes.tts: A trickle outward, about point three. Absorbing would pile protein up and stop itself. If water stopped moving, protein would seep out until the hold-back vanished.
scenes.narration: A trickle outward, about 0.3. Absorbing would pile protein up and stop itself. If water stopped moving, protein would seep out until the hold-back vanished.
scenes.caption: A trickle outward, about 0.3. Absorbing would pile protein up and stop itself. If water stopped moving, protein would seep out until the hold-back vanished.
scenes.visual: The question card dissolves; the word 'filter' stays and glows. A small label at the probe reads 'film protein: 11.9'. The GOLD bar settles at 12.7 (0.9 x (26 - 11.9)) beside the WHITE bar at 13; label 'net +0.3 out'. One slow BLUE drop leaves outward. A BLUE point is plotted at (12, +0.3), just above zero, well above the ORANGE point at -5. On 'stop itself', a brief dashed ghost: BLUE drops move in, GOLD piles under the mat, the inflow stops. On 'if water stopped moving', a second ghost: the BLUE drops freeze, GOLD dots seep out through the gap and the GOLD bar shrinks toward zero; then the ghost fades and the real trickle continues.

scenes.tts: At the arterial end, faster filtering rinses harder, so the hold-back grows. The net there falls from fifteen to about twelve. In this simple teaching model, every point filters.
scenes.narration: At the arterial end, faster filtering rinses harder, so the hold-back grows. The net there falls from 15 to about 12. In this simple teaching model, every point filters.
scenes.caption: At the arterial end, faster filtering rinses harder, so the hold-back grows. The net there falls from 15 to about 12. In this simple teaching model, every point filters.
scenes.visual: The probe slides back to the arterial end: BLUE drops pour out fast, label 'film protein: 2.6', the GOLD bar rises to 21.1 (0.9 x (26 - 2.6)) beside the WHITE bar at 33; label 'net about +12'. A BLUE point is plotted at (32, +12), just below the ORANGE point at +15. On 'every point filters', the probe sweeps right along the tube and BLUE points appear at (24, +4), (20, +1.6) and (16, +0.6); at every point the BLUE drops leave OUTWARD, thinning toward the venous end but never reversing. Tag 'illustrative model' joins 'teaching numbers' at bottom right.

scenes.tts: Plotted, the textbook line runs straight into absorption. The steady curve bends near twenty-two and flattens just above zero. That shape is the hockey stick.
scenes.narration: Plotted, the textbook line runs straight into absorption. The steady curve bends near 22 and flattens just above zero. That shape is the hockey stick.
scenes.caption: Plotted, the textbook line runs straight into absorption. The steady curve bends near 22 and flattens just above zero. That shape is the hockey stick.
scenes.visual: On 'textbook line', the dashed ORANGE line pulses and its part below zero (from 17 to 12) is shaded ORANGE, label 'absorbs'. On 'steady curve', a solid BLUE curve joins the BLUE points (32, +12), (24, +4), (20, +1.6), (16, +0.6), (12, +0.3): steep on the left, bending near 22 (small tick labelled 'bend ~22'), then running flat just above the zero line to the right, never crossing it. On 'hockey stick', the label 'hockey stick' appears beside the BLUE curve. In the tube above, BLUE drops keep leaving all along its length.

scenes.tts: Single frog capillaries held at low pressure absorbed only briefly. Then fluid movement fell to near zero, or slight filtration. Nearly all this evidence is from animal vessels.
scenes.narration: Single frog capillaries held at low pressure absorbed only briefly. Then fluid movement fell to near zero, or slight filtration. Nearly all this evidence is from animal vessels.
scenes.visual: Tag 'single frog capillaries' at top left. On 'held at low pressure', the WHITE push arrow at the probe shrinks sharply and a short burst of BLUE drops moves INTO the tube; a small timer beside the probe reads 'time (schematic)'. As GOLD collects under the mat (shown in a small circular inset of the gap), the inward burst slows and stops; on 'slight filtration', a thin trickle of BLUE drops leaves outward again. On 'animal vessels', a small tag 'animal data' appears beside the plot and stays.

scenes.tts: So in most tissues, the protein's pull can brake the outflow, but not turn it around for long. The leaked fluid needs another way home.
scenes.narration: So in most tissues, the protein's pull can brake the outflow, but not turn it around for long. The leaked fluid needs another way home.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the full world. On 'brake the outflow', the GOLD bar and the BLUE curve on the plot glow together; on 'not turn it around', the ORANGE shaded 'absorbs' region fades away. On 'another way home', BLUE drops collected in the tissue band drift toward the bottom edge of the band, and a small white arrow pointing off the bottom of the frame appears with a '?' beside it.

End card over the dimmed but still moving world (blood flowing left to right, BLUE drops leaving all along the tube, the BLUE hockey-stick curve on the plot). Large white text, centred: 'Protein can slow filtration, but cannot reverse it for long.'
